name: Hybrid Cloud
description: A pattern for workloads that span both on-premises infrastructure and cloud services, connected through secure networking. Common in government where legacy systems cannot be migrated immediately, data sovereignty requires on-premises hosting, or a phased cloud migration strategy is in progress.
whenToUse: Phased cloud migration where some workloads remain on-premises during transition
Data sovereignty requirements mandating certain data remains on-premises
Legacy systems that cannot be migrated but need to integrate with cloud services
Workloads requiring burst capacity in cloud while maintaining on-premises baseline
Organisations with existing on-premises investment that cannot be immediately decommissioned
whenNotToUse: New greenfield services with no on-premises dependency — use cloud-native instead
Workloads that can be fully migrated to cloud without hybrid complexity
Scenarios where the cost and complexity of hybrid networking is disproportionate
Small-scale services where maintaining two environments is operationally burdensome
Services where latency between on-premises and cloud would degrade user experience

typicalComponents.name: Hybrid Network Connectivity
typicalComponents.purpose: Provide secure, reliable connectivity between on-premises and cloud environments
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Direct Connect, Azure ExpressRoute, or Cloud Interconnect

typicalComponents.name: VPN Backup
typicalComponents.purpose: Provide encrypted backup connectivity if dedicated links fail

typicalComponents.name: Identity Federation
typicalComponents.purpose: Extend on-premises identity to cloud services for seamless authentication
typicalComponents.technology: AD Federation, Azure AD Connect, or Cloud Identity Federation

typicalComponents.name: Hybrid DNS
typicalComponents.purpose: Resolve names across on-premises and cloud environments
typicalComponents.technology: Route 53 Resolver, Azure Private DNS, or Cloud DNS forwarding

typicalComponents.name: Integration Middleware
typicalComponents.purpose: Bridge communication between on-premises and cloud-hosted services
typicalComponents.technology: API Gateway with VPN backend, Service Bus, or MQ

typicalComponents.name: Unified Monitoring
typicalComponents.purpose: Provide single-pane visibility across on-premises and cloud infrastructure
typicalComponents.technology: Datadog, Dynatrace, or cloud-native with on-premises agents

securityControls: Encrypt all traffic between on-premises and cloud using IPsec or MACsec
Implement network segmentation with firewall rules at the hybrid boundary
Extend identity and access management consistently across both environments
Implement consistent security monitoring and SIEM across hybrid estate
Apply zero-trust principles — do not assume trust based on network location
Regularly audit hybrid network connectivity for unauthorised access paths
Implement data classification to determine which data can traverse the hybrid boundary
resilienceConsiderations: Dedicated connectivity (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute) with VPN failover for redundancy
Design for graceful degradation if connectivity between environments is lost
Implement health checks that detect cross-environment connectivity failures
Consider data replication strategy for services spanning both environments
Plan for scenarios where cloud services are available but on-premises is not, and vice versa
Test failover between primary and backup connectivity regularly
costConsiderations: Dedicated connectivity has significant monthly port and data transfer costs
Running infrastructure in two environments increases overall operational costs
On-premises hardware refresh cycles continue alongside cloud consumption costs
Hybrid networking equipment and configuration management adds complexity costs
Factor in the cost of maintaining skills for both on-premises and cloud operations
Plan for eventual full migration to reduce long-term hybrid overhead
operationalConsiderations: Team must maintain expertise in both on-premises and cloud operations
Change management must coordinate across both environments
Monitoring must provide unified visibility across the hybrid estate
Incident response procedures must cover cross-environment failure scenarios
Capacity planning needed for both on-premises hardware and cloud resources
Migration roadmap should define timeline for reducing hybrid complexity

services.name: Azure Arc
services.purpose: Manage on-premises resources through Azure control plane

services.name: Azure AD Connect
services.purpose: Identity synchronisation between on-premises and cloud

services.name: Anthos
services.purpose: Manage workloads across on-premises and cloud

questionsToAsk: What workloads must remain on-premises and why (technical, regulatory, or commercial)?
Is there a migration roadmap to reduce hybrid complexity over time?
What bandwidth and latency requirements exist between on-premises and cloud?
Is dedicated connectivity (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute) already provisioned?
How will identity and access management work across both environments?
What is the disaster recovery strategy for the hybrid connectivity itself?
commonMistakes: Treating hybrid as a permanent architecture rather than a transitional state with a migration plan
Not implementing redundant connectivity, creating a single point of failure at the network boundary
Assuming on-premises security controls automatically extend to cloud resources
Underestimating the operational complexity of managing two distinct environments
Not implementing unified monitoring, creating blind spots at the hybrid boundary
